tier_reason: C stands: first-party book sample run, code only in the repo.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Book sample run (relayed via seed lead, not on a repo page): binary search 24.2 ns versus linear search 471 ns for the fixed needle 2137 in a 10M-element vector, so the about 19x (derived) compares a 2,138-element linear scan that stops at index 2137 with a 24-probe binary search, not a full 10M scan; with the needle at the end of 10M elements (main_4) about 24 ns versus 2.8 ms, about 117,000x (derived).
corrections.caveats: Enricher: main_1..3 fix the needle at 2137, so for n >= 1e4 std::ranges::find always stops at index 2137 and the linear series is flat from 1e4 to 1e7; the earlier caveat that the speedup grows with n holds only for main_4. Every iteration repeats the same needle (warm cache and a repeating branch pattern); main_4's needle is int64_t against a vector<int>, and the Catch2 variant narrows a size_t needle to int. The repo's CI builds only Chapter10/customer; Chapter13 is never CI-built.

tier_reason: D stands: no speedup attributable to musttail.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: every benchmarked factorial returns 0 (for n >= 66 the product holds 64 factors of 2 and uint64 wraps; the timing is still valid); iteration::fibonacci(1) returns 0, a bug outside the benchmark. The macro named musttail rewrites later [[gnu::musttail]] spellings, and MSVC still builds optimization_1 with an empty macro. The harness is Release-only at shallow depth, so the stack-depth benefit of musttail is never shown. Chapter13 is never CI-built.
